skill.displayName: Workplace Group Stress Heatmap | 职场员工压力群体热力图

llm.summary: This skill needs careful review because it sends sensitive workplace camera media to a cloud API while silently creating and persisting account-linked identities despite anonymity claims.

dimensions.detail: The skill handles highly sensitive workplace surveillance footage, reads local uploaded video files or accepts remote URLs, sends them to lifeemergence cloud endpoints, reads a workspace identity file if present, and has limited scoping or confirmation around cloud storage and report retrieval.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time backdoor, remote code execution, scheduled task, or tool replacement was found; the package uses Python scripts and ordinary dependencies, though one requirements file names yaml==6.0.3 while the code uses PyYAML.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs automatic triggering for office-camera videos and historical-report keywords, automatic local attachment handling, mandatory cloud querying, and silent identity initialization that must not be shown to the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Runtime code creates a workspace data directory and SQLite database, provisions or reuses a default user, and stores account fields plus access/open tokens for later report association; this is persistent credential and identity state, not system-level persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is anonymous, group-level workplace stress heatmaps, and remote media analysis/history retrieval can fit that purpose, but the implementation is a generic cloud API wrapper whose actual analysis and retention behavior are opaque and tied to internal user/report identity.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm that your organization has employee notice and consent, understands that videos or URLs are sent to a third-party cloud service, and accepts local/remote account-linked report history. Do not treat the skill as fully anonymous unless the provider documents retention, access controls, deletion, and proof that employee-level identifiers or small-group re-identification are not possible.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The artifact does use a shared/generic backend API wrapper rather than local heatmap logic, but cloud API analysis is disclosed and can be purpose-aligned; this supports opacity/under-disclosure concern, not a malicious finding by itself.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Verified: the documentation and code silently resolve an open_id, read data/smyx-api-key.txt, create a fallback User_ identity, and use that identity for historical report access, which conflicts with the plain anonymity framing.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Verified: the local sys_user model includes username, realname, email, token, and open_token, and RequestUtil can provision a remote account and persist returned tokens; account auth may be operationally useful but is under-disclosed for an anonymous workplace-analysis skill.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill relies on broad file, network, and local database access without a narrow permission boundary or named allowed domains beyond configuration, which matters because the handled data is workplace camera footage.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The notes mention consent and non-use for performance evaluation, but the overview and automatic workflows still underplay the employment, consent, and surveillance risks for stress inference from fixed office cameras.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Verified: the skill repeatedly says it does not identify individuals, while a separate internal workflow creates or reuses durable account identifiers and associates reports with them; this is contradictory unless clearly limited to administrator/service identity.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Verified: office-camera videos and broad history-report phrases can trigger processing or cloud report lookup automatically; that is too broad for sensitive workplace footage and retained surveillance-derived reports.
